brief.headline: Lead with supply security and a backup plan — they're in the distress zone and losing money, so push gently for ₹3.37 L in savings and faster cash

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹1.62/NOS price Bprex Pharma Packaging gives us on the LDPE bottle, and close the 4.3% gap
priceAsk.target: ₹3.37 L annual saving by matching our best price of ₹1.62/NOS
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited ₹1.62/NOS for the same LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE; Berry charges ₹1.69/NOS — a 4.3% gap. They're a pure reseller (100.0% traded, 0.0% made), so their price carries a middleman margin; push to the maker's price or switch more volume to Bprex.

paymentTermAsk.summary: They want cash badly (it's stuck for 335d vs 70d for similar firms) — offer to pay 15 days faster in exchange for part of the ₹3.37 L price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹3.34 L of our cash, but their cash crunch is worse than ours — trade speed for a discount roughly the size of their 2.77% borrowing cost

brief.financialLeverage: Berry Global India is in serious trouble: they lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24 (keeping -199.2% of every rupee they sell vs 2.3% for similar firms), owe 220.44 times their own cash, and sit in the distress zone (score -0.18). Their cash is stuck for 335d vs 70d for peers, so they're desperate for faster payment. We're 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue — big enough to matter, but not so big we can squeeze hard without risking supply. Since they make nothing themselves (100.0% traded), we're paying a reseller markup. The play: ask firmly but don't corner them; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek now so we can shift volume if they stumble.

evidence.figure: ₹-22.50 Cr final profit, -199.2% kept vs 2.3% for similar firms

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than rivals
evidence.figure: 335d cash stuck vs 70d for similar firms

evidence.point: We're a big slice of their sales
evidence.figure: ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They're a pure reseller, not a maker
We're paying 4.3% more than our best price on the main bottle
evidence.figure: ₹1.69/NOS vs ₹1.62/NOS at Bprex, gap 4.3%, ₹3.37 L annual excess

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — makes pharma bottles and caps in-house, a direct second source

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-packaging leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) — strong backup for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already gives us ₹1.62/NOS on the LDPE bottle (our best price) — shift more volume their way if Berry won't match

risks: They're losing money and in distress — pushing too hard could tip them over and kill our supply; keep Manjushree or Mold-Tek ready to take volume
They're a reseller, not a maker (100.0% traded) — any price cut eats straight into their thin margin; they may not be able to go lower without walking away
Their money-health score is 1/10 and they owe 220.44 times their own cash — watch for late deliveries or quality slips as they scramble for cash
We're 7.21% of their revenue — they need us, but if we yank the business suddenly they fold and we're stuck short
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but we're paying ₹1.69 when Bprex gives us ₹1.62 for the same bottle — let's close that 4.3% gap and talk about how faster payment from us helps your cash flow.
